brief: The Fed hiked in September, more hawkishly than Goldman Sachs expected, so GS now forecasts another hike in October, though it does not ultimately expect further hikes because its 2026/2027 core PCE forecasts (3.2%/2.2%) sit below the median FOMC dot (3.4%/2.5%). The ECB also hiked and GS expects a December hike, with a low hurdle for more if Euro area growth holds and inflation persists; the energy price surge is pushing GS to cut its 4Q26/1Q27 Euro area growth forecasts and raise its peak inflation forecasts. GS expects a BoJ hike this week, no faster pace, and the next hike in January 2027, watching whether Governor Ueda signals faster hikes, which would strengthen the yen. The BoE held rates but GS expects a November hike as energy pressures persist. This central-bank hawkishness is lifting global bond yields; GS raised its Bund and Gilt YE26 forecasts and sees Treasury yield risk skewed higher. Separately, GS cut its 2026 China GDP forecast on weak domestic demand, but flags Chinese firms' growing ex-China market share as a bright spot, expecting further gains even as expansion slows.
